'''Veselin Jungić''' (born June 12, 1955) is a Canadian [[mathematician]] who is a [[professor emeritus]] of mathematics at the [[Simon Fraser University]], in its Department of Mathematics. His research interests are in [[Ramsey theory]] and [[Mathematics education|mathematical education]].

== Early life and education ==
Veselin Jungić was born in the city of [[Banja Luka]] in former [[Yugoslavia]] and completed his undergraduate degree in mathematics at the [[University of Sarajevo|University of Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina]], earning a Bachelor of Science in 1977. He then pursued a master's degree in mathematics at the [[Faculty of Science, University of Zagreb]] in Croatia. In 1992, Jungić and his family moved to [[Vancouver|Vancouver, British Columbia]], to escape the [[Bosnian War]]. He continued his academic journey in mathematics, earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D]]. in 1999 from Simon Fraser University under the supervision of [[Tom Brown (mathematician)|Tom Brown]]. His Ph.D. thesis was titled ''Elementary, Topological, and Experimental Approaches to the Family of Large Sets''.<ref>{{cite thesis
|last= Jungić
|first= Veselin
|date= 1999
|title= Elementary, Topological, and Experimental Approaches to the family of Large Sets
|url= https://www.proquest.com/docview/304561478
|degree= PhD
|isbn=978-0-612-51878-0
|id= {{ProQuest|304561478}}
}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After completing his Ph.D., Jungić began his academic career in Canada as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|Postdoctoral]] Fellow in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of British Columbia]] under the supervision of [[David William Boyd]]. From 2001 to 2006, he served as a [[lecturer]] at Simon Fraser University's Department of Mathematics. In 2007, he was promoted to [[Senior lecturer|Senior Lecturer]] in the same department. In 2015, Jungić was appointed Teaching Professor at Simon Fraser University, a position he held until his retirement in 2025.

Jungić's academic research primarily focuses on [[Ramsey theory|Ramsey Theory]]. In one of his early papers, ''Rainbow Arithmetic Progressions and Anti-Ramsey Results'',<ref>{{Cite journal

|journal=Combinatorics, Probability and Computing

|volume=12
|issue=5–6
|pages=599–620
|doi=10.1017/S096354830300587X|url-access=subscription
}}</ref> Jungić and a group of researchers explored rainbow Ramsey Theory, investigating the existence of rainbow arithmetic progressions, where each element is a distinct color. The paper demonstrates that any 3-coloring of the [[natural number]]s, with each color appearing at least 1/6 of the time, must contain a 3-term rainbow arithmetic progression. The study extends these findings to similar colorings of the integers and discusses the broader implications for anti-Ramsey theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jungić |first1=Veselin |last2=Nešetřil |first2=Jaroslav |last3=Radoičić |first3=Radoš |date=2005 |title=Rainbow Ramsey Theory |url=https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/a9int2003/a9int2003.pdf |journal=Integers: Electronic Journal of Combinatorial Number Theory |volume=5 |issue=2 |doi=10.5281/zenodo.7948593}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Landman |first1=Bruce M. |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/stml-73 |title=Ramsey Theory on the Integers |last2=Robertson |first2=Aaron |publisher=American Mathematical Society |year=2014 |isbn=978-0-8218-9867-3 |edition=2nd}}</ref>

== Math Catcher Outreach program ==
Since its inception in 2011, the Math Catcher Outreach program, developed by Jungić, has aimed to promote mathematics among [[Elementary school|elementary]] and [[high school]] students by demonstrating its relevance in everyday life and decision-making. The program places a strong emphasis on [[Indigenous education in Canada|Indigenous education]], creating learning resources in various [[First Nations in Canada|First Nations]] languages.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Jungić |first1=Veselin |last2=MacLean |first2=Mark |date=2010 |title=Adventures of Small Number: A collection of short stories |url=https://www.sfu.ca/~vjungic/Small-Number/book-1.html}}</ref> It includes original stories, problem-solving activities, and hands-on tasks, ensuring that math education is enjoyable, inclusive, and culturally relevant for young learners. [https://www.google.com/maps/d/edit?mid=12IkRTShtyG7A6MMaoq7MJL9GU7YSVgnv&ll=16.887810937895942%2C-104.17303904999994&z=3 '''Map of the places visited by the Math Catcher Outreach Program''']

== Awards and honours ==
Veselin Jungić was inducted into the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]]'s 2021 Class of Fellows, recognizing his significant contributions to mathematics education, research, and service within the Canadian mathematical community. This Fellowship honors members who have demonstrated excellence in their field and provided distinguished service to Canada's mathematical community, highlighting Jungić's ongoing commitment to advancing mathematics education.

In 2020, Veselin Jungić received the [[Adrien Pouliot Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 3, 2020 |title=Veselin Jungic Receives the 2020 Adrien Pouliot Award |url=https://cms.math.ca/news-item/veselin-jungic-receives-the-2020-adrien-pouliot-award/ |publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society}}</ref> for his outstanding contributions to mathematics education, particularly through his leadership in the Math Catcher Outreach Program and initiatives that enhance learning experiences for Canadian post-secondary students. He co-organizes the Teaching Matters Seminar Series<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 28, 2019 |title=Teaching Matters Seminar Series: CEE What We're All About: A Conversation with Elizabeth Elle and the Centre for Educational Excellence Leadership Team |url=https://events.sfu.ca/event/8042-teaching-matters-seminar-series-cee-what-were-all |publisher=Simon Fraser University}}</ref> at Simon Fraser University and collaborates on educational initiatives like the "First Year Math and Stats in Canada"<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Burazin |first1=Andie |last2=Jungić |first2=Veselin |last3=Lovrić |first3=Miroslav |title=Three Countries, Two Continents: Common Challenges and Opportunities in Teaching First-Year Mathematics |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202001/rnoti-p64.pdf |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |publication-date=2020 |volume=67 |issue=1 |pages=64–67}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=First-Year Math & Stats in Canada |url=https://firstyearmath.ca/ |access-date=August 29, 2024 |website=FYMSiC}}</ref> program.

In 2015, Veselin Jungić was awarded the [[3M Teaching Fellow|3M National Teaching Fellowship]], a highly respected recognition for excellence in educational leadership and teaching at the university and college level. Conferred by [[List of higher education associations and organizations in Canada|the Society for the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning in Higher Education (STLHE)]], this Fellowship acknowledges Dr. Jungić's exceptional contributions to teaching and learning in Canadian post-secondary education. As a recipient, Jungić became a member of the STLHE Council of Fellows, joining a distinguished group of educators committed to advancing the quality of education in Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Council of National Fellows for Excellence in Teaching and Learning |url=https://www.stlhe.ca/council-of-national-fellows-for-excellence-in-teaching-and-learning/ |access-date=Aug 29, 2024 |website=Society for Teaching and Learning in Higher Education}}</ref>

Veselin Jungić was awarded the 2012 CMS Excellence in Teaching Award<ref>{{Cite web |date=Feb 21, 2012 |title=BC Professor Recognized as Exceptional Math Educator: Veselin Jungic to Receive the 2012 CMS Excellence in Teaching Award. |url=https://www2.cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2012/et-announcement |publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society}}</ref> for his innovative contributions to undergraduate mathematics education at Simon Fraser University. His pioneering use of online tools in large [[calculus]] classes, along with his dedication to student success and integration of Indigenous culture into mathematics education, underscores his effectiveness as an educator.

In 2011, Veselin Jungić received the PIMS Education Prize from the [[Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 29, 2011 |title=SFU's Veselin Jungic awarded 2011 PIMS Education Prize |url=https://pims.math.ca/news/2011/03/sfus-veselin-jungic-awarded-2011-pims-education-prize |publisher=Pacific Institute for the Mathematical Sciences}}</ref> for his role in enhancing public awareness and appreciation of mathematics. His contributions include leading educational programs like "Taste of Pi<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jungić |first=Veselin |title=A Taste Of Pi - Talks and Activities for High School Students |url=https://www.sfu.ca/~vjungic/Atasteofpi.html |access-date=August 29, 2024}}</ref>" for high school students, mentoring Indigenous students, and creating the animated film "Small Number Counts to 100,<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Jungić |first1=Veselin |last2=MacLean |first2=Mark |last3=Roy |first3=Simon |title=Small Number Counts to 100 |url=https://www.sfu.ca/mathcatcher/StoriesMovies/CountsTo100.html |access-date=August 29, 2024}}</ref>" which integrates [[Indigenous storytelling in North America|Indigenous storytelling]] into mathematics lessons.

== Other publications ==
In 2023, Veselin Jungić published ''Basics of Ramsey Theory'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=Jungić |first=Veselin |title=Basics of Ramsey Theory |publisher=Chapman and Hall/CRC |year=2023 |isbn=9781003286370 |edition=1st |location=New York |pages=1–238 |doi=10.1201/9781003286370}}</ref> an introductory textbook aimed at undergraduate students. The book is designed to introduce readers to Ramsey theory, a mathematical field at the intersection of number theory and combinatorics.

In the same year, Jungic co-authored a textbook on differential calculus with Petra Menz and Randall Pyke, both from Simon Fraser University. The book offers over 900 problems covering key topics like [[Limits of integration|limits]], [[Continuity equation|continuity]], [[derivative]]s, and their applications, including [[Mathematical optimization|optimization]] and curve sketching.

Veselin Jungić is the creator and producer of the podcast ''[https://open.spotify.com/show/4UrTrYkJc9rFhiOQRoNbm3 No Strangers At This Party]'', which celebrates Ramsey theory and the mathematicians working in this vibrant field. The podcast features interviews with contemporary mathematicians who are actively engaged in Ramsey theory, discussing their early experiences with mathematics, their academic journeys, and their perspectives on Ramsey theory and mathematics as a whole.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jungić |first=Veselin |date=November 2024 |title=No Strangers at This Party |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202410/noti3054/noti3054.html?adat=November%202024&trk=3054&pdfissue=202410&pdffile=rnoti-p1331.pdf&cat=none&type=.html |journal=American Mathematical Society |volume=71 |issue=10}}</ref>

Jungić has contributed several writings addressing key issues in education, including the significance of mathematics, personal academic challenges, and the impact of academic dishonesty. Through a combination of personal reflection and professional insight, these works highlight the importance of integrity, perseverance, and the role of mathematics in developing critical thinking skills. His writings advocate for a deeper understanding of the educational process and the promotion of academic honesty.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Burazin |first1=A. |last2=Jungić |first2=V. |last3=Lovrić |first3=M. |date=September 2020 |title=Let them cheat: Why it's tempting for college and university instructors to look the other way |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/opinion/opinion-academic-cheating-1.5576990 |work=CBC News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jungić |first=Veselin |date=September 2019 |title=Math, a necessary subject - Interview, by Harry Jing |url=https://thelasource.com/en/2019/09/09/math-a-necessary-subject/ |work=The Source}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jungić |first=Veselin |date=2019 |title=My experience as a 'dumb' student |url=https://universityaffairs.ca/opinion/in-my-opinion/my-experience-as-a-dumb-student/ |work=University Affairs}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Jungić |first=Veselin |date=January 2020 |title=A math teacher's plea: Let's keep pi irrational |url=https://theconversation.com/a-math-teachers-plea-lets-keep-pi-irrational-127159 |work=The Conversation}}</ref>
